''16. The {{ls}}pirit giueth te{{ls}}timonie.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The te{{ls}}timonie of the Spirit.}}This place maketh not for the Heretikes {{ls}}pecial faith, or their pre{{ls}}umptuous certainty that euery one of them is in grace: the te{{ls}}timonie of the Spirit being nothing els, but the invvard good motions, comfort, and contentment, vvhich the children of God do daily feele more and more in their hartes by {{ls}}eruing him: by vvhich they haue as it vvere an atte{{ls}}tation of his fauour tovvardes them, vvhereby the hope of their iu{{ls}}tification and {{ls}}aluation is much corroborated and {{ls}}trengthened.

''17. Yet if they {{ls}}uffer.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Novvith{{ls}}tandĩg Chri{{ls}}ts {{ls}}atisfaction and Pa{{ls}}sion, yet ours al{{ls}}o is required.}}Chri{{ls}}tes paines or pa{{ls}}{{ls}}ions haue not {{ls}}o {{ls}}atisfied for al, that Chri{{ls}}tian men be di{{ls}}charged of their particular {{ls}}uffering or {{ls}}atisfying for eche mans ovvne part: neither be our paines nothing vvorth to the attainement of heauen, becau{{ls}}e Chri{{ls}}t hath done ynough. but quite contrarie: he vvas by his pa{{ls}}{{ls}}ion exalted to the glorie of heauen: therfore vve by compa{{ls}}{{ls}}ion or partaking vvith him in the like pa{{ls}}{{ls}}ions, {{ls}}hal attaine to be fellovves vvith him in his kingdom.

''18. Condigne.''] Our Aduer{{ls}}aries ground hereon, that the vvorkes or {{ls}}ufferances of this life be not meritorious or vvorthy of life euerla{{ls}}ting, vvhere the Apo{{ls}}tle {{ls}}aith no {{ls}}uch thing, no more then he {{ls}}aith that Chri{{ls}}ts Pa{{ls}}{{ls}}ions be not meritorious of his glorie, vvhich I thinke they dare not much auouch in our Sauiours actions. {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Al {{ls}}uffering in this life is nothing in compari{{ls}}on of the heauenly glorie: and yet it is meritorious & vvorthy of the {{ls}}ame.}}He expre{{ls}}{{ls}}eth onely, that the very afflictions of their ovvne nature, vvhich vve {{ls}}uffer vvith or for him, be but {{ls}}hort, momentanie & of no account in compari{{ls}}on of the recompen{{ls}}e vvhich vve {{ls}}hal haue in heauen. no more in deede vvere Chri{{ls}}tes paines of their ovvne nature, compared to his glorie, any vvhit comparable: yet they vvere meritorious or vvorthy of heauen, & {{ls}}o be ours. And therfore to expre{{ls}}{{ls}}e the {{ls}}aid compari{{ls}}on, here he {{ls}}aith, ''They art not condigne'' {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=* ''ad gloriam''. {{lang|grc|πρὸς τὴν μέλλουσαν δόξαν}}}}''to the glorie''. He {{ls}}aith not, ''of the glorie'', as the Heretikes fal{{ls}}ly tran{{ls}}late: {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Heretical tran{{ls}}lation.}}though the Scripture {{ls}}peaketh {{ls}}o al{{ls}}o, vvhen it {{ls}}ignifieth only a compari{{ls}}on. as ''Prou. 3''. in the greeke, ''Omne pretio{{ls}}um non e{{ls}}t'' {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''* {{lang|grc|ἄξιον ἀυτῆς}}''}}''illa dignum''. S. Augu{{ls}}tine, ''illi dignum''. S. Hierom, ''non valet huic comparari''. that is, No pretious thing is vvorthie of vvi{{ls}}edom, or to be compared vvith it. See the like ''Eccle. 26, 20. Tob. 9, 2''. But vvhen the Apo{{ls}}tle vvil expre{{ls}}{{ls}}e that they are condigne, vvorthy, or meritorious of the glorie, he {{ls}}aith plainely, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''2. Cor. 4, 17''.}}''That our tribulation vvhich pre{{ls}}ently is momentanie and light, vvorketh aboue mea{{ls}}ure exceedingly an eternal vveight of glorie in vs''. The valevv of Chri{{ls}}tes actions ri{{ls}}eth not of the leingth or greatnes of them in them {{ls}}elues, though {{ls}}o al{{ls}}o they pa{{ls}}{{ls}}ed al mens doings: but of the vvorthines of the per{{ls}}on. {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Vvhence the merite of vvorkes ri{{ls}}eth.}}And {{ls}}o the value of ours al{{ls}}o ri{{ls}}eth of the grace of our adoption, vvhich maketh tho{{ls}}e actions that of their natures be not meritorious nor an{{ls}}werable to the ioyes of heauen in them {{ls}}elues, to be vvorthy of heauen. And they might as vvel proue that the vvorkes of {{ls}}inne do not demerite damnation. for, {{ls}}inne in deede for the quantity and nature of the vvorke is not an{{ls}}werable in plea{{ls}}ure to the paine of Hel: but becau{{ls}}e it hath a departing or auer{{ls}}ion from God, be it neuer {{ls}}o {{ls}}hort, it de{{ls}}erueth damnation, becau{{ls}}e it alvvaies procedeth from the enemy of God, as good vvorkes that be meritorious, procede from the childe of God.

''24. By hope vve are {{ls}}aued.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=As {{ls}}ometime faith only is named, {{ls}}o els where only hope, and only charitie, as the cau{{ls}}e of our {{ls}}aluation.}}That which in other places he attributeth to faith, is here attributed to hope. for when{{ls}}oeuer there be many cau{{ls}}es of one thing, the holy writers (as matter is mini{{ls}}tred and occa{{ls}}ion giuen by the doctrine then handled) {{ls}}ometimes referre it to one of the cau{{ls}}es, {{ls}}ometime to an other: not by naming one alone, to exclude the other, as our Aduer{{ls}}aries captiou{{ls}}ly and ignorantly do argue: but at diuers times and in {{ls}}undrie places to expre{{ls}}{{ls}}e that, vvhich in euery di{{ls}}cour{{ls}}e could not, nor needed not to be vttered. In {{ls}}ome di{{ls}}cour{{ls}}e, faith is to be recommended: in others, charitie: in an other, hope: {{ls}}ometimes, almes, mercie: els where, other vertues. One while, ''Euery one that beleeueth, is borne of God. 1 Io. 5, 1''. An other while, ''Euery one that loueth, is borne of God. 1 Io. 4, 7''. Sometimes, faith purifieth mans hart. ''Act. 15, 9''. And an other time, Charitie remitteth {{ls}}innes. ''1 Pet. 4, 8''. Of faith it is {{ls}}aid, ''The iu{{ls}}t liueth by faith. Ro. 1, 17''. Of charitie, ''We knovv that vve are transferred from death to life, becau{{ls}}e we loue &c. 1 Io. 3, 14''.

''27. The Spirit de{{ls}}ireth.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Scripture abu{{ls}}ed again{{ls}}t the Godhead of the Holy Gho{{ls}}t.}}Arius and Macedonius old Heretikes had their places to contend vpon, again{{ls}}t the Churches {{ls}}en{{ls}}e, as our nevv Mai{{ls}}ters now haue. They abu{{ls}}ed this text to proue the Holy Gho{{ls}}t not to be God, becau{{ls}}e he needed not to pray or a{{ls}}ke, but he might commaund if he vvere God. Therfore S. Augu{{ls}}tine expoundeth it thus, ''The Spirit prayeth''. that is, ''cau{{ls}}eth and teacheth vs to pray, and vvhat to pray or a{{ls}}ke''. Augu{{ls}}t. de anima & eius orig. li. 4, c. 9. & ep. 121. c. 15.

''30. Whom he hath prede{{ls}}tinated.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The doctrine of prede{{ls}}tination, how to be reuerenced, and what it teacheth vs.}}Gods eternal fore{{ls}}ight, loue, purpo{{ls}}e, prede{{ls}}tination, and election of his deere children, and in time their calling, iu{{ls}}tifying, glorifying by Chri{{ls}}t, as al other actes and intentions of his diuine wil and prouidence towardes their {{ls}}aluation, ought to be reuerenced of al men with dreadful humilitie, and not to be {{ls}}ought out or di{{ls}}puted on vvith pre{{ls}}umptuous<noinclude>{{continues|boldnes}}</noinclude>
